entries.name: a2a
entries.description: PiG that speaks A2A (Agent2Agent): call remote A2A agents from tools, and serve PiG tasks to A2A agents when you configure a listener. Off until configured.
notes: Source only: no Piglet Binary is published and no remote installation command is offered yet. See the root RELEASE-BLOCKERS.md.
The A2A listener is off unless a2a.json, PIG_A2A_LISTEN or --a2a-listen configures it, and it refuses to start without authentication tokens.
The extension is Go and fuses into the Piglet Binary; it depends on the upstream a2a-go v2.6.0 (Apache-2.0).
Also selected by pig-with-batteries; the listener is off there too until configured.

The manifest lists five build targets, but only linux/amd64 has been built and run; linux/arm64, darwin/arm64, darwin/amd64 and windows/amd64 are listed in the manifest and compile-checked only, so no platform is a support claim.

entries.name: acp
entries.description: PiG for editors: an agent that an Agent Client Protocol client such as Zed drives through the pig-acp companion, with /acp to show how to configure it.
notes: Source only, Go only. Lets an editor that speaks the Agent Client Protocol (Zed and others) drive a PiG agent: the Package components/acp is a Go port of pi-acp (Sergii Kozak, MIT).

The Piglet Binary does not speak ACP by itself. ACP is JSON-RPC on stdio and a fused extension must not write protocol bytes to the host's stdout, so the entrypoint is the companion executable pig-acp, started by the editor with --pig pointing at this agent. Proven with a built Piglet Binary as the --pig target of pig-acp (11 end-to-end scenarios and the ACP reference client); there is no one-command Binary yet.

Advertised and implemented: initialize, session/new, session/load, session/list, session/delete, session/prompt with streaming text, thoughts, tool calls, diffs and terminal output, session/cancel, model and thinking-level selection, context usage, permission requests for extension select and confirm dialogs. Not supported, by design: file system and terminal delegation, MCP servers passed by the editor, extension slash commands, input and editor dialogs.

No release is published; version 0.1.0 is a development default and only linux/amd64 has been built and run; linux/arm64, darwin/arm64, darwin/amd64 and windows/amd64 are listed in the manifest and compile-checked only; neither is a support claim.

entries.name: herdr
entries.description: PiG with the herdr agent-state reporter: idle, working and blocked in herdr's sidebar, notifications and `herdr agent wait`.
notes: Optional: the reporter is the standalone extension Package components/herdr, which works on its own in plain PiG without this Piglet.
Source only: no Piglet Binary is published and no remote installation command is offered yet. See the root RELEASE-BLOCKERS.md.

The extension does nothing unless PiG runs inside a herdr pane (HERDR_ENV=1 with HERDR_PANE_ID, HERDR_BIN_PATH and HERDR_SOCKET_PATH set), as herdr's published integration guide (https://herdr.dev/docs/add-herdr-support/) requires.

With herdr 0.9.2 or later it also reports the resume command `pig --session <session file>`, so herdr restores the pig session in its pane after a server restart. The restore runs plain `pig` (no Piglet or launch flags), and an in-memory session reports no command. Older herdr keeps the state reports and the release; the resume command is left out.
It is a Go extension on PiG's public SDK: building the Piglet needs a Go toolchain, not Node.js. It does not honor the Pi-only herdr:blocked event, because the Go SDK has no pi.events bridge.

A local Piglet Binary builds with the reviewed PiG and reports to a fake herdr, but none is signed or published. The manifest lists five build targets, but only linux/amd64 has been built and run; linux/arm64, darwin/arm64, darwin/amd64 and windows/amd64 are listed in the manifest and compile-checked only, so no platform is a support claim.

entries.name: jev
entries.description: PiG with Jev, a typed judge for tool calls and tool output (destructive? leaks data? beyond scope? secret in the output?). Off until you run /jev on, which shows what leaves the machine first; it fails open.
notes: Optional: the judge is the standalone extension Package components/jev, which works on its own in plain PiG without this Piglet.

Off by default. Nothing is judged and nothing is sent until you run /jev on (which shows what leaves the machine and where) or set "enabled": true in your own pi-jev.json. A key in the environment or a file in a repository never turns it on.
The judge is the model PiG is configured with (default) or the TypeSafe API, through the shared Go client Package components/typesafe. Content goes to that provider; /jev names it.
Fails open: when the judge is unavailable, tool calls run unjudged. A judgment is probabilistic advice, not a sandbox.

Source only: no Piglet Binary is published and no remote installation command is offered yet. See the root RELEASE-BLOCKERS.md. The manifest lists five build targets, but only linux/amd64 has been built and run; linux/arm64, darwin/arm64, darwin/amd64 and windows/amd64 are listed in the manifest and compile-checked only, so no platform is a support claim.

entries.name: pig-extension-porter
entries.description: Port a Pi TypeScript extension to a Go PiG extension: SDK gap check, tests first, differential equivalence against the original, mutation check, binary build and a Package with provenance.
notes: Source only, Go only. The focused porter for Pi TypeScript extensions: the strict porting Skill plus the equivalence harness as a fused Go extension. Run npm run stage before using its generated manifest under dist/staged.
Most users who port extensions want this Piglet rather than pig-porter, which extends it. Its Packages (extension-port, extension-equivalence) also install on their own with pig install.

A Piglet Binary builds locally from the staged manifest with PIG_SOURCE_ROOT set to a git checkout of the PiG source. No release is published; version 0.1.0 is a development default and only linux/amd64 has been built and run; linux/arm64, darwin/arm64, darwin/amd64 and windows/amd64 are listed in the manifest and compile-checked only; neither is a support claim.

entries.name: pig-games
entries.description: PiG with two pixel-art games, PiG Runner (/runner) and Angry Pigs (/angry-pigs), starring the pig you chose with PiG's /sprite. Nothing starts until you type a command.
notes: Source only, Go only. Two pixel-art games, PiG Runner (/runner, /pig-runner) and Angry Pigs (/angry-pigs), moved from PiG Standard (Michael Kinsy, MIT). They draw the pig chosen with PiG's built-in /sprite (PiG 0.4.0 and later), so the Piglet bundles no login of its own. Run npm run stage before using its generated manifest under dist/staged.

Nothing starts by itself. The games register only their commands and no event handler (PIG_GAMES_MCP=1 adds a session_start handler for the opt-in agent server; /runner mcp on and /angry-pigs mcp on serve a game to an agent on 127.0.0.1 behind a random token, off by default). Both Packages (pig-runner, angry-pigs) also install on their own from a Pigpen checkout; each needs the pig-play sprite library beside it (../pig-play).

A Piglet Binary builds locally from the staged manifest with PIG_SOURCE_ROOT set to a git checkout of the PiG source. No release is published; version 0.1.0 is a development default and only linux/amd64 has been built and run; linux/arm64, darwin/arm64, darwin/amd64 and windows/amd64 are listed in the manifest and compile-checked only; neither is a support claim.

entries.name: pig-porter
entries.description: Port Pi work to native PiG. Today that is Pi TypeScript extensions to Go, through the pig-extension-porter composition it extends.
notes: Source only, Go only. The umbrella porter: it extends pig-extension-porter (PiG's extends), so it carries the same porting Skill and Go equivalence extension without a copy. Run npm run stage before using its generated manifest under dist/staged.
Most users porting a Pi extension should use pig-extension-porter. This is not PiG's core parity-maintenance porter. No public release or Piglet Binary is available.
pig piglet add cannot copy an extends closure, so it is not installable remotely today. See RELEASE-BLOCKERS.md.

entries.name: pig-typesafe
entries.description: The typesafe_evaluate tool and /typesafe command (Go port of pi-typesafe). Off until enabled; content goes to api.typesafe.ai unless the own-model backend (the model PiG is configured with) is selected.
notes: Source only, Go only. Selects the pi-typesafe Package: the typesafe_evaluate tool and the /typesafe command, off until the operator enables them. Run npm run stage before using its generated manifest under dist/staged.
Content submitted goes to api.typesafe.ai unless the own-model backend is selected, which sends it to the provider of the model PiG is configured with. The Piglet says which in its consent dialog.

A Piglet Binary builds locally from the staged manifest with PIG_SOURCE_ROOT set to a git checkout of the PiG source. No release is published; version 0.1.0 is a development default and only linux/amd64 has been built and run; linux/arm64, darwin/arm64, darwin/amd64 and windows/amd64 are listed in the manifest and compile-checked only; neither is a support claim.

entries.name: pig-warden
entries.description: PiG with warden: irreversible calls held before they run, off-task calls flagged, stuck loops and unverified done claims called out. Off until /warden enable; it shows what leaves the machine before anything does; judged by TypeSafe Jev or your own session model.
notes: Source only, Go only. Warden, a Go port of DevMortimer's pi-warden (Ryan Gapac, MIT): irreversible tool calls held before they run, off-task calls flagged, stuck loops and unverified done claims called out. Run npm run stage before using its generated manifest under dist/staged.

Opt-in: it does nothing until /warden enable, which shows what would leave the machine and asks which judge to use: TypeSafe Jev, your own session model, or offline patterns only. The warden Package also installs on its own with pig install and shares the typesafe client library Package.

A Piglet Binary builds locally from the staged manifest with PIG_SOURCE_ROOT set to a git checkout of the PiG source. No release is published; version 0.1.0 is a development default and only linux/amd64 has been built and run; linux/arm64, darwin/arm64, darwin/amd64 and windows/amd64 are listed in the manifest and compile-checked only; neither is a support claim.

entries.name: pig-with-batteries
entries.description: The batteries-included Piglet: default PiG with curated extensions. Today: the herdr agent-state reporter, the read_session tool, the /context, /tools, /cost and /prompts inspection commands, PiG Runner (/runner) and Angry Pigs (/angry-pigs), the Pig Snake game (/pig-snake), which start only on their command, the pig-doctor /doctor command (nothing runs unless you invoke it), Jev, a typed judge for tool calls that is off until you run /jev on, the a2a Package (A2A tools; its listener stays off until you configure it), and the websearch first slice (search, fetch, retained sources). Protocol bridges and more capability ports are planned.
notes: Source only, not the finished batteries-included composition. It selects the herdr agent-state reporter (Package components/herdr, Go), PiG Runner and Angry Pigs (Packages pig-runner, angry-pigs, Go, moved from PiG Standard; they draw the pig chosen with PiG's built-in /sprite), the Pig Snake game (Package components/pig-snake, Go, starts only on /pig-snake), the read_session tool (Package components/session-ingest, Go), the /context, /tools, /cost and /prompts commands (Package components/context-info, Go; its footer is opt-in), the pig-doctor /doctor command (Package components/pig-doctor, Go; command only, nothing runs automatically), the a2a Package (Package components/a2a, Go: A2A tools, listener off until configured), the websearch first slice (Package components/websearch, Go: web_search, fetch_content, get_search_content, source_check, web_enable; the rest of pi-web-access is deferred and named in its PORT.md), plus an empty build-pipeline fixture (seed-check, Go). The roadmap is approved; capability ports are pending implementation.

The games start only on their command (/runner, /pig-runner, /angry-pigs, /pig-snake). Bundling is not activating. The sprite login and /sprite are PiG's own (built in since 0.4.0); this Piglet no longer bundles one.

It also selects Jev (components/jev), a typed judge for tool calls and output. Selectable and off by default: nothing is judged or sent until you run /jev on, which shows what leaves the machine and where. It fails open. The standalone jev Piglet and this one both build a Binary locally.
The herdr reporter does nothing unless PiG runs inside a herdr pane. Every extension in this Piglet is Go, so it needs no Node.js.

A local Piglet Binary builds with the reviewed PiG, but none is signed or published. The manifest lists five build targets, but only linux/amd64 has been built and run; linux/arm64, darwin/arm64, darwin/amd64 and windows/amd64 are listed in the manifest and compile-checked only; the targets and the 0.1.0 version are not a support or release claim.
Newer PiG builds support subdirectory source add and per-Piglet release tags, but this composition is not published and no installation command is offered yet. See RELEASE-BLOCKERS.md.
